idiom_name: one Java package per module; package-private (default) access for internals
implementation_notes: The classic Java module is a package: package com.acme.billing; with the published types declared public and everything else left at default (package-private) access, which is exactly the visible-inside-the-module-only level the pattern needs - no modifier keyword required. Sub-packages are not part of their parent package, so com.acme.billing.internal is a different module; internals that must be reachable from the package body have to live in the same package and be non-public. package-info.java documents the module and packages map onto directories under the source root, so the folder layout can mirror the model.
pitfalls: Sub-packages do not inherit access: helper classes placed in a child package become a second module and package-private members are unreachable across the boundary.
Classpath mode and reflection (setAccessible, automatic modules) defeat package encapsulation at run time; if the boundary must hold, the application has to run on the module path.
Package-private is invisible to tests in other packages, which pushes teams towards making internals public - a test fixture that lives in the module's own package keeps the boundary intact.

variants.name: JPMS module: module-info.java declaring the published packages
variants.implementation_notes: Since Java 9 a module can be a named module: module-info.java lists requires and exports, so only exported packages are visible to other modules and that encapsulation is enforced at compile time and run time - the closest Java equivalent of the pattern's published interface. The same file makes the dependency graph explicit, which turns cycles into build errors. The cost is module-path packaging, no split packages, and frameworks that reflect on domain types needing explicit opens directives.
pitfalls: Reflective frameworks (ORM, JSON mapping, dependency injection) need opens directives and fail with strong encapsulation until they are added.

Migrating a classpath application piecemeal produces automatic modules whose names come from JAR file names and which export everything, so the boundary is nominal until the whole graph is modularised.
